      "observations": [
        "All owned hunks in 23 paths were read. Cargo.lock adds dependency metadata matching the Graph Cargo.toml additions; it is not handwritten style or a build result. The URI and URL-listener moves are distinct: SafeUri differs only in pub(crate)→pub visibility, proved by exact normalized bytes, while SafeUrlListener changes from an EWS wrapper alias to its own RefPtr-backed shared struct.",
        "The new Graph bridge still stores ExchangeConnectionDetails during Initialize. CheckConnectivity unwraps those details, makes a return URI and detaches client work. The ordinary VerifyLogon caller obtains a protocol client through GetProtocolClient, whose new-client path calls Initialize before returning. Direct use before initialization is not guarded in this original bridge; the fixed client getter returns NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED.",
        "The initial client constructs another SafeUri for callbacks, calls OnStartRunningUrl, selects AboutMe from /me, sends the request and reports success/error with OnStopRunningUrl. The URI returned by the bridge is not the awaited HTTP result. The two original SafeUri::new calls are separate construction sites; fixed bridge code instead passes a URI clone into the later operation handler.",
        "The historical transport uses operation.build for its URI but always calls moz_http client.get. It obtains credentials, adds Authorization only when supplied, handles 4xx/5xx as ProtocolError::Http and otherwise deserializes GraphResponseType with serde_json. It does not send the generated PATCH method/body. Existing generator and typed PATCH lessons stay separate from this first transport implementation.",
        "The endpoint path is copied, a slash is pushed and the generated request URI is appended. The generated /me path already starts with a slash, so the pre-join string has adjacent slashes for a /v1.0 configured path. This is a static string-construction observation, not a reproduced server failure or a claim about URL normalization. The original transport inserts no v1.0 literal; current base_api_url explicitly appends the version and current generated requests trim trailing separators.",
        "Moving SafeListenerWrapper and its traits wholesale was deferred. The EWS SafeListener implementation for the moved URL listener remains in the EWS connectivity module. The original shared URL listener exposes an unsafe raw-listener clone accessor with a temporary-use warning; the private EWS UnsafeListener adapter is its stated caller. SafeListenerWrapper and handle_error become pub(crate). Current accepted shared code later uses the generic wrapper alias and common safe-listener framework.",
        "The moved URL-listener comments still name SafeListenerWrapper and Self::on_success/on_failure even though this original file now has a distinct struct and the trait implementation stays in EWS. Those comments must be read with the actual implementation; no rustdoc failure was reproduced. The two reviewer clippy suggestions are adopted as direct map_err enum constructors in the exact original Graph client.",
        "No tests change or are added in this patch. Prior generated request tests establish request shape only; the new HTTP/authentication/status/deserialization path has no new direct assertion here. The full review provides manual setup steps and a reviewer historical success report, not a fresh test or security guarantee. Upstream Rust/XPCOM and HTTP crate implementations remain bounded dependencies.",
        "Read the complete retained primary Bug1995825 current0–2, activity and actual footer. The description proposes /me if possible and folder listing otherwise; exact landed source selects /me, so the fallback proposal is not credited as implemented. Dependency2008752, Graph phase1 and later2010053 remain metadata-only locators.",
        "The full own D277114 review was read in the B collector with 13 actual inlines and no summary edits. The author moves from a constant API-version prefix idea to requiring the configured URL to include /v1.0. Typed API-version work and autodiscover remain follow-ups. Reviewer historical manual success is separate from our static audit.",
        "The source adopts both direct map_err enum-constructor suggestions and the interim unsafe-listener warning/private EWS adapter. It does not move the whole safe-wrapper framework. The fixed accepted shared alias, client initialization guard, API-version insertion and queued operation flow are later phases. No new account, authentication, network, test, build or lint run occurred."
